### LexiconCountVectorizer

>  LexiconCountVectorizer (feature_store:textplumber.store.TextFeatureStore,
>                              lexicons:dict, lowercase:bool=True)

*A Sci-kit Learn pipeline component to get document-level counts for one
or more lexicons. This component should be used after the
SpacyPreprocessor component with the same feature store.*

### LexiconCountVectorizer.get_feature_names_out

>  LexiconCountVectorizer.get_feature_names_out (input_features=None)

*Get the feature names out from the vectorizer.*

Note: currently lexicon counts are not stored in the feature store. It
will be added in the future to avoid recomputing lexicon counts. A
feature store is still required, as this is the source of the tokens to
calculate counts.

### get_empath_lexicons

>  get_empath_lexicons (save_to:str|None='lexicons_empath.txt')

*Get the empath lexicons from the empath github repo.*

The [Empath library](https://github.com/Ejhfast/empath-client) provides
word lists corresponding to a number of lexical categories. These can be
loaded using
[`get_empath_lexicons`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#get_empath_lexicons)
to extract lexicon-based features from texts. There is an example below.
Here is a preview of the data …

``` python
empath_lexicons = get_empath_lexicons()
print('Empath lexicon examples: ')
for key in ['love', 'hate', 'help', 'sleep']:
    print(f'{key}: {empath_lexicons[key][0:5]} (First 5 tokens of {len(empath_lexicons[key])})')

print()
print('Avaliable lexicons: ')    
for i, key in enumerate(empath_lexicons.keys()):
    if i % 8 == 0:
        print()
    print(f'{key}, ', end='')
```

    Empath lexicon examples: 
    love: ['love', 'indulge', 'closeness', 'yearn', 'love'] (First 5 tokens of 86)
    hate: ['hate', 'despise', 'vindictive', 'infuriate', 'sexist'] (First 5 tokens of 102)
    help: ['help', 'chore', 'responsible', 'help', 'grateful'] (First 5 tokens of 60)
    sleep: ['sleep', 'sleepy', 'rest', 'sleep', 'bedroom'] (First 5 tokens of 53)

### get_sentiment_lexicons

>  get_sentiment_lexicons (save_to:str|None='lexicons_sentiment.txt')

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 6%" />
<col style="width: 25%" />
<col style="width: 34%" />
<col style="width: 34%" />
</colgroup>

<tbody>
<tr>
<td>save_to</td>
<td>str | None</td>
<td>lexicons_sentiment.txt</td>
<td>where to save the file, None will not save</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The
[`get_sentiment_lexicons`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#get_sentiment_lexicons)
function can be used to download positive and negative lexicons based on
words that are typically verbs or adjectives in the [Vader Sentiment
Lexicons](https://github.com/cjhutto/vaderSentiment). Vader’s valence
scores are based on human raters. The Vader lexicon already excludes
words with strong disagreement between raters. The
[`get_sentiment_lexicons`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#get_sentiment_lexicons)
function also filters out words where raters gave both positive and
negative valence scores. See the function code for details.

Note: when these lexicons are used with the
[`LexiconCountVectorizer`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#lexiconcountvectorizer),
the features returned are simple counts. It does not use Vader’s rules
or Vader’s valence scores. However, the Textplumber does implement VADER
as a feature extractor and estimator. See the
[`VaderSentimentExtractor`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/vader.html#vadersentimentextractor)
and
[`VaderSentimentEstimator`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/vader.html#vadersentimentestimator)
classes for more details.

Here is a preview of the positive and negative lexicons …

``` python
sentiment_lexicons = get_sentiment_lexicons()
print('Sentiment lexicon examples: ')
for key in ['positive', 'negative']:
    print(f'{key}:')
    print(f'{sentiment_lexicons[key][0:5]}')
    print(f'(First 5 tokens of {len(sentiment_lexicons[key])})')
```

    Sentiment lexicon examples: 
    positive:
    ['absolved', 'absolving', 'accept', 'acceptable', 'accepted']
    (First 5 tokens of 858)
    negative:
    ['abandon', 'abandoned', 'abandoning', 'abducted', 'abhor']
    (First 5 tokens of 1136)

## Example

Here is an example …

``` python
from textplumber.preprocess import SpacyPreprocessor
from textplumber.lexicons import LexiconCountVectorizer, get_empath_lexicons, get_sentiment_lexicons
from textplumber.store import TextFeatureStore
from textplumber.core import get_example_data
from textplumber.report import plot_confusion_matrix, plot_logistic_regression_features_from_pipeline

from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline, FeatureUnion
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
```

Here we load text samples from Barack Obama and Donald Trump available
in the [AuthorMix
dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/hallisky/AuthorMix).

``` python
X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, target_classes, target_names = get_example_data(label_column = 'style', target_labels = ['obama', 'trump'])
```

Create a feature store …

``` python
feature_store = TextFeatureStore('feature_store_example_lexicon.sqlite')
```

How accurately can we predict Obama or Trump using positive and negative
sentiment lexicons (from
[`get_sentiment_lexicons`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#get_sentiment_lexicons))?

``` python
sentiment_lexicons = get_sentiment_lexicons()
```

A
[`SpacyPreprocessor`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/preprocess.html#spacypreprocessor)
component must be included in the pipeline prior to the
[`LexiconCountVectorizer`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#lexiconcountvectorizer).

``` python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', SpacyPreprocessor(feature_store=feature_store)),
    ('lexicons', LexiconCountVectorizer(feature_store=feature_store, lexicons=sentiment_lexicons)),
    ('classifier', LogisticRegression(max_iter = 5000, random_state=55))
], verbose=True)

display(pipeline)
```

How does this compare to a model using features based on Empath’s
categories (using
[`get_empath_lexicons`](https://geoffford.nz/textplumber/lexicons.html#get_empath_lexicons))?

``` python
empath_lexicons = get_empath_lexicons()
```

Train a model using features based on counts for each Empath category.

``` python
pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('preprocessor', SpacyPreprocessor(feature_store=feature_store)),
    ('lexicons', LexiconCountVectorizer(feature_store=feature_store, lexicons=empath_lexicons)),
    ('classifier', LogisticRegression(max_iter = 5000, random_state=55))
], verbose=True)

display(pipeline)
```
